Corporate Profile 
WHO WE ARE
We are a global AI-native engineering services leader, where AI is 
the very foundation of how we design, build, and deliver intelligent 
solutions for our clients. We use AI and hyperspecialized industry 
expertise to engineer autonomous enterprises. 
At Coforge, we believe that the leaders of tomorrow will have their 
business capabilities defined and executed by a combination of 
humans and agents, underpinned by an enterprise data core and a 
cloud foundation purpose-built for AI. 
We combine AI agents with our AI-enabled workforce, including 
specialized FDEs in hybrid, pod-based delivery units. With a deep 
focus on trusted AI, our solutions are secure, governed, and 
enterprise-grade. 
We are outcome-led by design. Moving beyond AI experimentation, 
we deliver measurable business outcomes: lower operating costs, 
faster cycle times, higher conversion rates, and sustained margin 
growth.
OUR CORE VALUES
We engineer growth, which we measure in terms of our people, our 
clients’ businesses, and the communities that we are a part of.
We believe that sustained growth does not happen by accident. It 
is engineered.
We believe that growth and responsibility are not parallel paths, 
but the same journey.
We believe that growth must be accelerated, and purpose must 
be scaled, to create enduring value for business, society and the 
planet.
OUR VISION AND MISSION
Our vision is to “Engage with the Emerging.” We engage early and 
intensely with emerging technologies. We fuse human ingenuity 
and emerging technologies to guide the world’s leading enterprises 
to create enduring value.We lead with capabilities in AI-led engineering, cloud, and data 
technologies to help clients evolve into intelligent, high-growth 
enterprises.
Our mission is to “Transform at the Intersect,” helping our 
customers achieve their business objectives by combining our deep 
expertise in both technology and domain. We have applied this 
approach to provide business solutions within our chosen industry 
verticals: Banking and Financial Services, Insurance, Travel, Public 
Sector (outside India), Hi-Tech, and Healthcare.
COFORGE TODAY
We have a global presence across North America, South America, 
Europe, the Middle East, India, Asia-Pacific, and Australia. We drive 
operations from 54 global delivery centers across 32 countries. As 
of June 30th, 2026, we had over 40,000 AI engineers, technology 
and process experts who design, engineer, modernize, and operate 
client systems across the world.
We are focused and committed to our clients’ success, as reflected 
in our repeat business rate of 95% in FY26. We have an exceptional 
track record of execution, which has been a key enabler of robust 
and consistent revenue growth over the last nine years from INR 
27,558Mn in FY17 to INR 1,64,027Mn in FY26, with a 20.3% CAGR over 
this period. 
Following the closing of our Encora acquisition, our revenue run rate 
for FY27 is approximately $2.5 billion, out of which approximately $2 
billion is contributed by AI-led engineering, cloud, and data services.
We have strong partnerships with hyperscalers and other 
technology providers focused on AI, such as Pega and ServiceNow.  Corporate Profile

04 AI-First Engineering | Architecting the Agentic  EnterpriseWe have a robust set of AI assets and industry-domain focused AI 
solutions. Our AI specialists work with large enterprises to design 
and deliver enterprise-grade agentic AI solutions.
Coforge Nuuron, our AI operationalization platform, transforms 
enterprise knowledge, business context, and decision logic into an 
operational intelligence layer, helping enterprises deploy agentic AI 
solutions at scale with the necessary guardrails for compliance and 
risk management. 
• Our CodeInsightAI platform is a proven legacy modernization 
tool. 
• Our BlueSwan® platform is an end-to-end AI-driven quality 
engineering platform.
• Our EvolveOps.AI offering is an autonomous cloud 
infrastructure management platform that 37 of our clients 
are currently using to deploy AI agents for automated cloud 
operations. 
• Our agentic AI data assets enable data modernization, cloud 
migration and data ops.
• We have launched industry-domain focused AI platforms such 
as Nexa for insurance firms, and Aeronova.AI for airlines.
Below are a few examples of how clients benefit from our AI-led 
engineering capabilities and AI assets:
• A global travel technology provider that handles nearly one 
third of all airline bookings volume is using CodeInsightAI to 
modernize its mainframe applications and move them to 
cloud. 
• A global financial organization leveraged Coforge’s AI expertise 
to implement an AI-driven fraud detection and decisioning 
solution architected for real-time payments and enterprise-
grade scalability.
• A leading HR solutions provider is using Coforge’s Nuuron 
platform, including the AI gateway, Model Garden and Coforge 
AgentSphereTM, to implement a governed AI application 
development framework across the enterprise.We pride ourselves on strong employee engagement, resulting in 
a 10.8% attrition rate: one of the lowest levels and a testament to 
our company culture. 
This employee centricity was demonstrated again in 2026, 
when Coforge was recognized as a “Great Place to Work” for the 
sixth consecutive year.  We were also among the ET Edge Best 
Organisations for Women in 2026.
LOOKING FORWARD
As the shift to agentic AI continues, the most successful enterprises 
will harness intelligent systems to drive autonomous decisions. 
This means that AI platforms will be measured by how much they 
can be trusted, and value will be measured by the outcomes they 
deliver. 
We are already building our business for that future.
Coforge will continue our evolution to an AI-first, engineering-led 
enterprise, expanding our investments in next-generation delivery 
platforms, foundational agents, and hyper-specialized solutions 
built for the industries we serve. We will deepen our ecosystem 
partnerships to co-create high-impact solutions with the best in 
the industry, while cultivating an adaptable, agile, and AI-ready 
talent pool to face tomorrow’s challenges.
Above all, we will continue to anchor our growth in relationships, 
because true transformation isn’t transactional. It’s built over time, 
through trust, collaboration, and shared ambition.
That is what defines us. That is what drives us.
And, this is what enables Coforge to engineer the agentic 
enterprises of tomorrow.Corporate Overview                   Statutory Reports                    Financial Statements

Message from the CEO
SUDHIR SINGH
CEO & Executive Director
Dear Shareholders,
FY26 was a defining year for Coforge, not only because of the growth 
and profitability we delivered, but because of how we delivered it. 
The technology services industry is going through a genuine shift in 
its business model: from a scale-of-people business to a scale-of-
intelligence one, where how many people you can deploy matters 
less than the intelligence and judgment you bring to a client’s 
problem. Clients are moving away from paying for effort and 
toward paying for outcomes, risk reduced, revenue unlocked, value 
delivered on their terms. Our Forward Deployed Engineers (FDE) 
program is where this shows up most clearly: we embed elite, AI-
fluent engineers directly inside client environments, compressing 
the distance between problem and solution from months to weeks. 
This is the front line of our AI strategy, and it is changing how 
Coforge competes. 
Against this backdrop, FY26 was another exceptional year for 
Coforge, marked by industry-leading growth, sharply improved 
profitability, and continued progress on our long-term priorities. 
We delivered revenue growth of 29.2% over FY25 in USD terms, our 
second consecutive year of industry-leading growth, and our ninth 
consecutive year of robust, profitable growth overall. Over FY17 to 
FY26, revenue has grown at a CAGR of 20.3% and EBIT at a CAGR of 
24.6% in INR terms, a class-leading performance that has continued 
to accelerate even as our base has scaled.
Growth in FY26 was broad-based across every vertical, geography 
and service line, underpinned by our combination of deep 
engineering expertise and strong domain knowledge. FY26 saw             The technology services industry is shifting from 
a scale-of-people business to a scale-of-intelligence 
business. Our clients are no longer buying effort; they 
are buying outcomes. Coforge is built for this shift, 
combining AI, engineering depth, and domain expertise 
to deliver measurable business value at speed.
the highest-ever number of large deal wins in our history, and 
our next-twelve-months signed order book stood at USD 1.75 
billion, up 16.4% over FY25, giving us strong visibility into continued 
momentum in FY27. Profitability improved just as meaningfully. 
Our FY26 EBIT margin was 14.4%, up 370 basis points, driven in large 
part by the programmatic use of AI to lift the efficiency of our own 
internal operations. We do not just sell AI transformation. We run 
on it ourselves.
We also took a significant step toward our AI ambition this year 
with the acquisition of Encora, an AI-native engineering firm born 
in Silicon Valley. Together, Coforge and Encora will form a combined 
entity which will derive more than USD 2 billion in revenue from AI-
led engineering, Data and Cloud services alone. That differentiated 
core sets the foundation that will help us realize the potential of AI 
for enterprise clients across the world.  
The AI Opportunity
AI is redefining our industry at a pace the market has not seen 
before. Three shifts matter most for how we run Coforge: 
enterprise AI spend is scaling non-linearly as clients move from 
pilots to enterprise-grade agentic implementations; client buying 
behavior is shifting from headcount and capacity to outcomes, 
driving new commercial models such as outcome-based pricing 
and hybrid human-agent pods; and competitive moats are moving 
from scale to AI-specialist talent and deep engineering capability, 
as legacy delivery knowledge becomes less relevant.“
Another Exceptional Year of Industry-Leading GrowthCoforge is built for this moment. Our AI-led engineering depth, 
strong domain expertise and lack of any material legacy managed-
services drag give us a structural advantage. Competitors carrying 
large legacy books of run-the-business work will find it far harder 
to make this pivot than we will. Backed by our execution intensity, 
we have reimagined every dimension of our business to lead, not 
merely participate, in this next phase of growth. Three key pillars 
anchor this strategy:
1. Coforge Nuuron, our AI Operationalization Platform, was 
built to solve one of the biggest challenges in enterprise 
AI today: turning AI capability into repeatable business 
outcomes at enterprise scale.
• Organizations have accumulated vast amounts of 
intelligence across their systems, processes, data, and 
people. The opportunity has always been to apply 
that intelligence consistently across the thousands of 
decisions, workflows, and actions that drive business 
outcomes every day. Until recently, that has been difficult 
to achieve at enterprise scale, limiting the ability of 
organizations to fully realize the promise of AI. 
• Coforge Nuuron changes that. It transforms enterprise 
knowledge, business context, and decision logic into an 
operational intelligence layer that helps organizations 
make better decisions and achieve outcomes more 
predictably. 
• The platform is the culmination of years of our 
investments in AI-native assets including Coforge  
Forge-XTM, EvolveOps.AI, CodeInsightAI, Coforge Data 
CosmosTM, and BlueSwan®, bringing together the 
capabilities required to connect intelligence, workflows, 
decisions, and execution across the enterprise. 
• By turning intelligence into action, Coforge Nuuron 
enables a new model of enterprise operations - adaptive, 
autonomous, and outcome-driven.
2. An AI-native talent and delivery model. In FY26, we trained 
more than 30,000 engineers on AI technologies and delivery 
practices, creating one of the industry’s largest pools of 
AI-enabled engineering talent. At its leading edge is our 
specialized team of Forward Deployed Engineers who work 
alongside clients to rapidly identify opportunities, build 
solutions, and accelerate value realization. Complementing 
this is Mod Squads, our subscription-based delivery model that 
combines specialist engineering talent, pre-built AI agents, 
and reusable IP into dedicated outcome-focused teams. 
Together, these capabilities enable clients to move from idea 
to production faster, while maintaining a relentless focus on 
business outcomes rather than effort-based delivery.
3. Speed of value realization. Our Outcome Acceleration 
Framework is designed to shorten the path from AI 
deployment to measurable business impact. The biggest 
challenge is rarely the technology itself but embedding it into 
the way people work. An underwriting agent delivers little 
value if underwriters do not use it. A customer service copilot 
has limited impact if agents are not enabled and measured 
to adopt it. That is why we integrate workflow redesign, 
adoption, governance, and value measurement alongside 
the technology from day one. By treating these as a single 
workstream aligned to business outcomes, we help clients 
move beyond pilots faster and realize value with greater 
speed, predictability, and scale.
This is our answer to where the industry is heading: clients are 
buying outcomes, not capacity, and demanding a speed of execution 
legacy models cannot match. Our Forward Deployed Engineer 
model exists to meet that demand: our best AI engineering talent, 
embedded in client systems, delivering outcomes in weeks rather 
than quarters. This is fast becoming core to how Coforge competes, and I expect it to be one of our most important differentiators as 
more large deals get structured around FDE-led pods rather than 
traditional staffing.
This momentum shows up in independent analyst recognition too. 
In FY26, Coforge earned 25+ AI recognitions from leading analyst 
firms, including seven “Leader” designations. Everest Group 
named us a Leader in AI Services, HFS Research an Innovator using 
AI, Avasant Group a Disruptor in AI Services, ISG a Rising Star in 
AI Deployment, and NelsonHall a Leader in AI Capabilities. What 
matters most is that these recognitions consistently point to the 
same thing our clients tell us directly: that Coforge knows how to 
turn AI capability into deployed, working outcomes faster than 
most of the industry.
People and Culture
Our people remain the cornerstone of everything we have built. In 
FY26, our employee base reached 35,777, with 2,754 net additions. 
What I am proudest of is not the size of that number, but what sits 
behind it: on the back of a genuinely people-focused culture, we 
retained one of the lowest attrition rates in the industry at 10.8%. 
The addition of Encora brings approximately 9,500 people into the 
Coforge family, including more than 3,500 engineers across Latin 
America and Eastern Europe, expanding both our delivery footprint 
and the diversity of our talent base. As AI reshapes what it means 
to do engineering work, our priority is to make sure our people are 
its authors, not spectators, which is why AI-linked career tracks, 
continuous upskilling and the Forward Deployed Engineer pathway 
are as much a people strategy as a technology one.
This culture continues to be recognized externally: we were 
awarded the “Great Place to Work” certification for the fifth year 
in a row, and named among the ET Edge Best Organisations for 
Women 2026, reflecting our sustained focus on gender diversity, 
inclusive leadership and equitable career progression. None of this 
happens by accident. It is the result of treating culture with the 
same discipline we bring to our P&L.
Outlook
Looking ahead, we remain laser-focused on extending our growth 
leadership into FY27 and beyond, anchored in our differentiated 
capabilities and execution intensity. The technology services 
industry is at an inflection point, where the capabilities that define 
a leader are being rewritten in real time, and we intend to be one 
of the organizations doing the rewriting. Our Forward Deployed 
Engineer model, our Coforge Nuuron platform, and our conviction 
that clients will increasingly buy outcomes rather than capacity are 
not side bets; they are the operating logic of Coforge going forward.
We remain confident of robust, sustainable growth in the years 
ahead, and determined to emerge from this AI era even stronger, 
as one of the planet’s most trusted innovation and transformation 
partners for enterprises. The conversation around AI is often 
centered on models, platforms and tools; at Coforge, we see it 
in a broader sense, as a force multiplier for human potential, 
enabling our people to work smarter, deliver faster and create 
more meaningful impact for our clients. That is the Coforge we are 
building, and I have never been more confident in our ability to get 
there.
On behalf of the Board and the leadership team, I extend my 
sincere gratitude to our clients, employees, partners, investors 
and all stakeholders for their continued trust and support. Every 
milestone we achieve reflects your confidence in us and the 
commitment of our teams around the world.
SUDHIR SINGH
Chief Executive Officer & Executive Director

FY26 Overview
FY26 represents a year of strong execution and increasing strategic 
momentum for Coforge, as the Company continues to scale its 
presence in large, transformation-led engagements across key 
markets. Growth during the year was driven by consistent deal wins, 
expansion within existing accounts, and participation in complex, 
multi-year programs aligned with enterprise modernization 
priorities. The Company maintained its growth trajectory on the 
back of a robust order pipeline and a high-quality executable order 
book of USD 1.75 billion for the next twelve months as of Q4 FY26, 
reflecting a 16.4% year-over-year (YOY) increase. 
This performance was supported by sustained large deal 
momentum. This included USD 2.26 billion of order intake in FY26, 21 
large deals signed during the year, and a steady cadence of multi-
region deal closures across North America, Europe and APAC. For 
FY26, Coforge reported consolidated revenue of USD 1.87 billion, 
reflecting 29.2% YoY growth in USD terms. This builds on a strong 
FY25 base of USD 1.45 billion in annual revenue, positioning the 
Company for sustained growth and scale.  The year also reflected 
strong operating leverage, with EBIT margin expanding by 370 
basis points YoY to 14.4%, while profit after tax increased to USD 
177.4 million.
Coforge enters FY27 with enhanced visibility and confidence in its 
growth trajectory, supported by a USD 1.75 billion executable order 
book, a healthy large-deal pipeline, and increased participation in 
strategic transformation programs. The Company’s performance 
continues to be anchored in a differentiated operating approach 
that combines deep domain specialization with disciplined 
execution. A focused emphasis on high-quality engagements, 
outcome-driven delivery, and long-term client partnerships 
has resulted in improved revenue predictability, stronger client 
stickiness, and a more resilient growth profile.Coforge’s performance continues to be anchored in a differentiated 
operating approach that combines deep domain specialization with 
disciplined delivery. The Company has maintained a sharp focus on 
fostering quality client engagements, prioritizing opportunities 
where it can deliver measurable business outcomes, and building 
long-term strategic relationships. This has resulted in improved 
revenue visibility, stronger client stickiness, and a more resilient 
growth profile.
Coforge’s ability to combine deep domain expertise with 
engineering-led execution has enabled it to meaningfully 
participate in this shift . The Company continues to deepen client 
relationships, improve engagement quality, and expand wallet 
share across key accounts, resulting in stronger revenue visibility 
and a more resilient growth profile.
As enterprise adoption of AI moves from experimentation to 
production, clients are prioritizing partners who can take end-
to-end ownership of systems, including their ongoing operation, 
governance, and optimization. This is expanding the scope of 
engagements toward long-duration, managed services-led 
programs with higher value realization over time. Coforge’s AI-
led engineering approach, supported by a growing portfolio of 
proprietary platforms, accelerators, and domain-centric IP, has been 
a key enabler of this shift. These capabilities are being embedded 
across the lifecycle of engagements to accelerate modernization, 
improve delivery productivity, and enhance outcome predictability. 
Rather than being positioned as standalone solutions, these assets 
are increasingly driving differentiation in large deal pursuits, 
enabling faster time-to-value and supporting Coforge’s ability to 
execute complex, transformation-led programs at scale.
As the Company moves into FY27, it does so from a position of 
strength. The strategic focus remains on scaling AI-powered 
solutions, expanding client wallet share, and delivering margin-
accretive growth through disciplined execution. With a strong 
executable order book, a resilient and diversified client base, 
and a differentiated portfolio aligned to the evolving technology 
landscape, Coforge is well-positioned to sustain its growth 
momentum. FY26, in this context, represents a significant 
milestone that strengthens the foundation for the Company’s 
next phase of growth and its continued journey toward building 
intelligent, high-growth enterprises for its clients while creating 
long-term stakeholder value.Management Discussion & Analysis
08 AI-First Engineering | Architecting the Agentic  EnterpriseBusiness Overview
Coforge operates as a focused, AI-native engineering services 
leader, differentiated by its deep domain specialization, its 
engineering-led delivery model, and consistent execution in 
complex, large-scale transformation programs. The Company’s 
positioning is anchored in its ability to combine industry context 
with engineering depth, enabling it to deliver measurable business 
outcomes rather than effort-led services. Coforge continues to 
build on a strong foundation of sustained, high-quality growth, 
reinforcing its position as one of the fastest-growing digital 
engineering firms in the industry. The Company’s performance 
is underpinned by a focused strategy, consistent execution, and 
an increasing ability to participate in large, transformation-led 
engagements across key markets.  Over the years, the Company 
has evolved from a traditional technology services provider into 
a strategic transformation partner, helping clients solve complex, 
domain-specific challenges by integrating advanced technologies  
with deep industry expertise.
Coforge’s growth is anchored in three structural strengths. First, 
a deeply embedded execution discipline that drives consistency, 
predictability, and delivery excellence across engagements. 
Second, a strong large-deal engine focused on solution-led, multi-
year managed services programs, enabling the Company to expand 
wallet share and participate in strategic client initiatives. Third, a 
differentiated domain-led engineering approach, built on deep 
industry specialization, which allows Coforge to address complex, 
context-specific business challenges with precision.
Coforge’s operating model is built on the convergence of industry 
expertise and next-generation technology capabilities. Its offerings 
are centered on engineering, leveraging AI, cloud, data, integration, 
and automation to enable enterprise-wide transformation. AI has 
emerged as a structural growth driver. As enterprise adoption 
evolves from early generative AI use cases to more advanced, 
agentic, and autonomous systems, Coforge is positioned to capture 
this opportunity by embedding AI across the full lifecycle of client 
engagements. The Company’s platforms, including Data Cosmos, 
CodeInsightAI, Coforge QuasarTM, AI Studio, Coforge AgentSphereTM, 
GenAI Central, and Trust AI, are enabling scalable and responsible AI 
adoption, driving productivity gains and faster time-to-value while 
ensuring governance, security, and enterprise-grade reliability.
The integration of Cigniti Technologies represents a meaningful 
acceleration in Coforge’s growth and operating model, 
strengthening both capability depth and deal participation 
across large, enterprise-scale programs. More importantly, the 
integration is beginning to unlock strategic cross-sell opportunities 
across Coforge’s client base. While the initial performance has 
been driven largely by standalone momentum, the cross-leverage 
between Coforge’s engineering-led capabilities and Cigniti’s 
leadership in quality engineering is expanding deal sizes and 
increasing participation in multi-tower transformation programs. 
This combination enables Coforge to offer a more integrated 
value proposition across engineering, modernization, and AI-
led assurance, which is increasingly critical for enterprise-scale 
transformation. BlueSwan®, an AI-led next-gen digital assurance & quality engineering platform, further strengthens this positioning 
by enabling enterprise-wide, AI-led quality engineering and 
validation, supporting faster release cycles, higher automation, 
and improved delivery predictability. Together, the integration 
enhances Coforge’s ability to engage across the full lifecycle 
of transformation programs, while driving improved margins, 
stronger client stickiness, and a more scalable growth model.

AI-First Engineering | Architecting the Agentic  EnterpriseAI and Engineering as a Core Strategy 
The technology services industry is undergoing a structural 
realignment, as enterprise demand shifts from effort-based 
delivery toward engineering-led, AI-enabled value creation. This 
shift is redefining the basis of competitiveness, from scaling 
capacity to scaling outcomes, with an increasing emphasis on 
the ability to design, modernize, operate complex systems 
with precision, control, and continuity. As AI becomes integral 
to the technology stack, the primary driver of value is moving 
from development to lifecycle ownership, where governance, 
orchestration, and continuous optimization determine long-term 
impact.
In this environment, the distinction between linear delivery 
models and engineering-led execution is becoming increasingly 
pronounced. Enterprises are prioritizing partners that can move 
beyond program execution to assume accountability for system 
outcomes across build, run, and evolution. Coforge operates within 
this paradigm, with a delivery model architected to integrate AI 
into the core of engineering, enabling consistent execution at scale 
across complex, domain-intensive environments.
AI is now a foundational layer across the engineering lifecycle, 
enabling a transition from manual, artifact-driven processes to 
platform-enabled, agent-assisted execution. AI is embedded into 
modernization, development, quality engineering, and operations, 
driving a structural redesign of how enterprise systems are 
engineered and managed. The resulting model delivers not only 
improvements in productivity and cycle time, but also greater 
reliability, traceability, and operational control, which are critical to 
scaling AI in production environments.
At the center of this model is a platform-led execution architecture, 
where Coforge’s proprietary platforms and accelerators are deeply 
integrated into delivery. The Company’s One AI platform stack, 
including Coforge Quasar™, Coforge Forge-X™, CodeInsightAI, 
BlueSwan®, AIVA, Coforge Data Cosmos™, and EvolveOps.AI, acts 
as a unified engineering and AI fabric that enables industrialized 
transformation across the enterprise. This stack aligns with the 
Company’s broader AI value proposition across AI for Business 
and AI for Delivery, enabling enterprise-wide adoption while 
accelerating transformation delivery at scale.
Coforge Quasar™ provides an enterprise-grade AI foundation with 
multi-model orchestration, agentic frameworks, and embedded 
governance, enabling clients to deploy AI at scale without vendor 
lock-in. Coforge Forge-X™ drives AI-led engineering transformation 
by shifting delivery toward specification-driven and agent-
assisted execution. CodeInsightAI accelerates large-scale 
legacy modernization through AI-powered reverse and forward 
engineering, unlocking complex brownfield estates and enabling 
migration to modern architecture.
BlueSwan® injects AI into quality engineering by enabling high 
levels of automation, predictive quality, and continuous testing 
across programs. AIVA is one of the industry’s first composable 
agentic AI software development platform, enabling enterprises 
to assemble modular, reusable AI agents to execute complex 
business processes. Coforge Data Cosmos™ enables the creation 
of AI-ready, cloud-native data platforms that support enterprise-
wide AI adoption. EvolveOps.AI transforms run operations through 
AIOps, observability, and autonomous remediation, enabling 
intelligent, self-healing systems. Together, these platforms create 
a comprehensive, end-to-end transformation stack, that covers 
build, test, modernize, deploy, and run.
This platform ecosystem enables Coforge to move from bespoke, 
project-based execution to repeatable, IP-led delivery models that 
drive speed, consistency, and economic efficiency. Transformation 
programs are increasingly executed through reusable components, 
pre-built accelerators, and agentic workflows, enabling faster 
time-to-market and improved delivery predictability. This also strengthens Coforge’s ability to participate in large, multi-year, 
multi-tower engagements.
A key differentiator in this strategy is the integration of platforms 
with deep domain specialization. Coforge’s focus on select industries 
ensures that its AI and engineering capabilities are applied 
within real-world business contexts, regulatory environments, 
and operational workflows. This allows the Company to move 
beyond pilot-led AI adoption to production-scale, outcome-driven 
deployments across core enterprise systems.
The Company is also evolving its commercial model to reflect this 
shift. As AI changes the economics of delivery, the person-hour is 
becoming a less relevant unit of value creation. Coforge’s platform-
led and AI-augmented delivery constructs enable more modular, 
subscription-based, and outcome-linked models, improving 
alignment with client value while enhancing non-linearity in its 
own delivery engine. Constructs such as AI-powered Mod Squads 
further support this transition by combining domain-aligned 
engineering expertise with pre-built AI agents to deliver faster, 
more predictable outcomes. Importantly, Coforge’s model is 
designed to capture value across the full lifecycle of AI systems. As 
enterprises deploy agentic architectures at scale, the complexity of 
managing models, orchestrating agents, ensuring governance, and 
continuously optimizing systems creates a structurally expanding 
managed services opportunity. Coforge is positioned to own this 
layer through its platforms and engineering capabilities, extending 
its role from implementation to long-term lifecycle partner.
This strategy is underpinned by Coforge’s consistent emphasis on 
execution intensity and hyper-specialization. The Company’s ability 
to combine domain expertise with disciplined execution has been 
a key driver of its growth, and this continues to define how AI and 
engineering capabilities are operationalized across engagements.
Overall, Coforge is building a scaled AI-led engineering enterprise, 
where proprietary platforms, domain depth, execution rigor, and 
an AI-enabled workforce come together to deliver measurable 
business outcomes. This positions the Company strongly in a 
market that is increasingly rewarding firms capable of translating 
AI into real, production-grade impact.
Alliances and Partnerships 
Orchestrating a hyperscaler-centric AI ecosystem for scaled 
enterprise outcomes.
Coforge’s alliances and partnerships strategy is designed around 
a fundamental shift in the technology services landscape: Value 
is no longer created by isolated capabilities, but through the 
orchestration of integrated ecosystems that combine hyperscaler 
infrastructure, enterprise platforms, and AI-native innovation 
layers. In this evolving paradigm, Coforge is positioning itself not 
as a participant within partner ecosystems, but as an integrated 
AI-led transformation programs across enterprise ecosystems. At 
the foundation of this strategy lies Coforge’s deep and expanding 
engagement with leading hyperscalers, including Microsoft 
Azure, Amazon Web Services, and Google Cloud. During the year, 
Coforge also achieved Microsoft Solution Partner status across 
all six designations, further strengthening its hyperscaler-led 
transformation credentials. These relationships are structured 
as strategic growth engines, embedded across solution design, 
delivery, and commercialization. Coforge’s dedicated Strategic 
Growth Units aligned to hyperscalers enable co-innovation, joint 
solution development, and integrated go-to-market execution, 
ensuring that every transformation program is built on scalable, 
secure, AI-ready cloud foundations.
The Company’s hyperscaler partnerships are differentiated by 
their direct alignment with AI-led engineering transformation. 
Coforge integrates its proprietary platforms including, Coforge 
Quasar™, Coforge Forge-X™, and CodeInsightAI with hyperscaler-
native services such as Azure AI, AWS Bedrock, and Google Vertex AI to deliver enterprise-grade AI programs that move beyond 
experimentation to production-scale deployment. This tight 
coupling of hyperscaler capabilities with Coforge’s engineering IP 
enables clients to accelerate modernization, reduce time-to-value, 
and operationalize AI across the enterprise.
A defining element of Coforge’s alliance strategy is its early and 
deliberate alignment with the multi-model AI ecosystem. As 
enterprises increasingly adopt a portfolio approach to AI spanning 
multiple large language model (LLM) providers, Coforge enables 
seamless orchestration across models through Coforge Quasar™ 
platform, which acts as a control plane for multi-LLM integration, 
governance, and cost optimization. This approach ensures that 
clients retain flexibility, avoid vendor lock-in, and optimize AI 
adoption strategies based on workload-specific requirements.
Beyond hyperscalers, Coforge has built a layered ecosystem of 
enterprise platform partnerships that embed AI directly into 
business workflows. Strategic collaborations with Salesforce, 
ServiceNow, Appian, Snowflake, Databricks, and integration 
platforms such as Workato and SnapLogic enable Coforge to 
deliver end-to-end, AI-infused transformation across customer 
experience, operations, data, and enterprise systems. These 
partnerships are increasingly structured around joint solutioning 
and co-developed accelerators, enabling Coforge to integrate 
domain-specific intelligence directly into enterprise platforms.
Coforge’s partnership model is further strengthened by its focus 
on co-innovation and IP-led collaboration. The Company actively 
works with hyperscalers and platform partners to build joint 
accelerators, industry-specific agentic solutions, and reusable AI 
frameworks, significantly reducing deployment timelines while 
enhancing solution differentiation. This includes co-innovation 
initiatives such as the GenAI Center of Excellence (CoE) with 
ServiceNow, combining Coforge QuasarTM with Now Assist to 
accelerate enterprise AI adoption. This approach transforms 
partnerships from enablement channels into multipliers of 
innovation velocity and deal origination. 
The acquisition of Encora represents a strategic acceleration of 
this ecosystem-driven approach. Encora brings deep hyperscaler 
relationships, AI-native engineering capabilities, and the AIVA 
composable agentic AI platform architecture, enhancing Coforge’s 
ability to deliver large-scale, AI-led transformation programs 
across geographies. The combined entity strengthens Coforge’s 
positioning as a scaled AI-led engineering firm with a robust 
ecosystem backbone spanning hyperscalers, data platforms, and 
AI frameworks.
Looking ahead, Coforge is evolving its alliances strategy to align 
with the next wave of enterprise transformation defined by Agent-
as-a-Service models, autonomous workflows, and outcome-based 
commercial constructs. The Company is actively investing in co-
creating agentic ecosystems with hyperscalers, AI model providers, 
and platform partners, enabling the development of autonomous 
systems capable of executing complex, end-to-end business 
processes.

Global Economic Outlook and Industry Overview
The global economic environment continues to reflect steady yet 
uneven growth, shaped by moderating inflation, evolving trade 
dynamics, and persistent geopolitical uncertainty.
According to the International Monetary Fund (IMF), global growth 
is estimated at 3.4% in 2025 and is projected to moderate to 
3.1% in 2026, before recovering marginally to 3.2% in 2027. While 
inflationary pressures are gradually easing  and financial conditions 
remain broadly supportive, business sentiment continues to be 
influenced by elevated policy uncertainty and the risk of renewed 
trade disruptions. 
Growth trends remain divergent, with advanced economies 
expanding at a measured pace, while emerging and developing 
economies continue to demonstrate relatively stronger 
momentum, supported by domestic demand and increasing 
technology investments.
Within this macroeconomic context, enterprises are adopting 
a more disciplined and value-focused approach to technology 
spending. Investments are increasingly being directed toward 
initiatives that deliver measurable productivity gains, operational 
resilience, and long-term competitiveness. 
Technology-led investments, particularly in AI, cloud, data 
platforms, and digital infrastructure, are emerging as key enablers 
of growth, partially offsetting broader macroeconomic headwinds. 
At the same time, the external environment continues to 
present risks, including geopolitical developments, constrained 
fiscal capacity across certain economies, and prolonged policy 
uncertainty in key markets. This is accelerating a structural shift 
away from discretionary spending toward outcome-driven, 
engineering-led transformation programs that support cost 
optimization, scalability, and long-term competitiveness.
India continues to maintain a strong growth trajectory relative to 
global peers. As reflected in the IMF World Economic Outlook (April 
2026), India’s real GDP growth is estimated at 7.1% in 2024 and is projected to strengthen to 7.6% in 2025, before moderating to a still 
robust 6.5% in both 2026 and 2027. 
While the moderation reflects a gradual normalization following 
a period of strong expansion, India remains one of the fastest 
growing major economies, supported by resilient domestic demand, 
sustained public and private investment, and continued progress 
in digital infrastructure adoption. This favorable macroeconomic 
outlook continues to underpin enterprise confidence and 
technology spending, reinforcing India’s strategic importance 
as a key market for engineering led digital transformation and 
technology services.
Global Real GDP Growth 
Global Inflation 
Global inflation has continued a downward trajectory. Inflation 
declined from 5.8% in 2024 to 4.1% in 2025 and is expected to 
remain contained at around 4.4% in 2026, before easing further 
to 3.7% by 2027. This gradual disinflation is contributing to more 
stable financial conditions and improved visibility for enterprises, 
although inflation dynamics remain uneven across regions and are 
subject to ongoing policy and geopolitical risks.

According to Gartner (April 2026), worldwide IT spending is expected 
to grow by 13.5% in 2026, reaching approximately USD 6.31 trillion, 
driven by sustained momentum across AI infrastructure and 
software. This reinforces the structural shift toward AI-enabled 
platforms, digital engineering, and services-led transformation, 
with enterprise spending remaining resilient and increasingly 
focused on outcome-driven, high-impact initiatives despite 
prevailing macroeconomic uncertainty. Indian IT industry outlook
The Indian technology industry continues to demonstrate resilience 
and structural strength despite a dynamic global macroeconomic 
environment. 
As reported in the Nasscom Annual Strategic Review 2026, the 
Indian IT industry recorded growth of 6.1% in FY26, with total 
revenues exceeding USD 315 billion. This performance reflects the 
sector’s ability to adapt to evolving enterprise priorities, supported 
by the increasing industrialization of AI, convergence across IT 
services, business process management (BPM), and engineering 
research and development (R&D), and a sustained shift toward 
high-value, IP-led offerings. 
Engineering R&D and BPM have emerged as key growth drivers, 
while the continued expansion of global capability centers (GCCs) 
further reinforces India’s position as a global hub for digital 
innovation, engineering talent, and large-scale delivery.
Looking ahead, the industry outlook remains positive, anchored in 
structural demand for AI-led transformation, digital engineering, 
and outcome-driven technology solutions. AI is rapidly evolving 
from experimental deployments to becoming a foundational 
enterprise capability, with early adoption of agentic systems 
beginning to reshape execution models. This shift is driving 
increased demand for partners that combine deep domain 
expertise with advanced engineering capabilities. At the same time, 
the industry is transitioning from scale-led growth toward value 
creation, ecosystem-driven delivery, and long-term co-innovation 
models, positioning the Indian IT sector for sustained, high-quality 
growth in the years ahead.
The global macroeconomic environment remains mixed, with 
growth pressures in certain markets balanced by resilience in 
others. Despite this, enterprise technology investments remain a 
clear priority, particularly in AI, digital engineering, and productivity-
led transformation, as organizations focus on efficiency and cost 
optimization. This sustained focus is driving continued demand 
for high-value engineering-led services, positioning Coforge well 
to benefit from ongoing technology-led investments across key 
markets.

Coforge Forge-X™, and CodeInsightAI are not standalone offerings, 
but execution enablers that allow Coforge to industrialize 
transformation programs at scale.
Client relationships further reinforce this positioning. With 260+ 
clients, 95.5% repeat business, and a Net Promoter Score of 65, Coforge has built a high-trust engagement model characterized 
by longstanding relationships and expanding wallet share. This is 
complemented by a stable workforce with the lowest attrition in 
the industry, enabling continuity in delivery and deeper domain 
alignment.
Coforge’s operating model is structurally different. A relatively lean 
delivery pyramid, combined with increasing platformization, AI-
led execution, and an AI-enabled workforce, allows the Company 
to drive higher productivity and operating leverage.  This positions 
Coforge strongly in an industry, undergoing a fundamental shift 
from effort-based delivery to outcome-driven, AI-augmented 
engineering, where success is defined not by scale alone, but by the 
ability to engineer outcomes with precision and consistency.
Financial Performance
Coforge delivered exceptional financial performance in FY26, 
marked by robust revenue growth, significant margin expansion 
and improved profitability. Over the last 9 years Coforge has 
delivered a Revenue CAGR of 20.3%, EBIT CAGR of 24.6%, PAT CAGR 
of 24.1%, EPS CAGR of 22.0% and FCF CAGR of 18.9%. This shows the 
execution intensity of the company.

equivalent to USD 1.87 billion, reflecting year-on-year growth of 
35.9% in INR terms and 29.2% in USD terms. This performance 
was supported by sustained large-deal execution, broad-based 
growth across key verticals, expansion within strategic accounts, 
and continued demand for AI-led engineering, data, cloud and 
modernization services.
Profitability improved materially during the year. EBITDA stood 
at INR 30,464 million, growing 76.9% year-on-year. EBITDA margin 
expanded by 431 basis points year-on-year to 18.6%. EBIT stood 
at INR 23,645 million, growing 82.7% year-on-year. EBIT margin 
expanded by 370 basis points year-on-year to 14.4%, reflecting 
improved operating leverage, disciplined execution and the 
benefits of scale.
Profit after tax for FY26 stood at INR 15,557 million, growing 
91.6% year-on-year. The Company also delivered strong cash 
generation during the year, with free cash flow of USD 135.4 million, 
representing 68.4% year-on-year growth.
The fourth quarter reflected strong exit momentum. Revenue for 
Q4 FY26 stood at INR 44,504 million, equivalent to USD 489.1 million, 
growing 30.0% YoY in INR terms, 28.7% in constant currency terms, 
and 21.2% in USD terms. EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 
20.6%, while EBIT margin stood at 16.6%, representing the highest 
ever quarterly EBIT margin reported by the Company.Revenue mix
The revenue mix remained broad-based across verticals and 
geographies. For FY26, Banking and Financial Services contributed 
26.5% of revenue, Travel, Transportation and Hospitality 
contributed 23.0%, Insurance contributed 15.0%, Healthcare and Hi-
Tech contributed 10.8%, Government Overseas contributed 7.0%, 
and others contributed 17.7%. By geography, Americas contributed 
56.9% of FY26 revenue, EMEA contributed 28.9% and Rest of World 
contributed 14.2%.
By service offering, Engineering contributed 44.1% of FY26 revenue, 
Data and Integration contributed 21.5%, Cloud and Infrastructure 
Management Services contributed 18.4%, Intelligent Automation 
contributed 8.2%, and Business Process Management contributed 
7.9%. The balanced revenue profile across industries, geographies 
and service lines reinforces the resilience of Coforge’s operating 
model and the increasing relevance of its AI-led engineering 
portfolio.

Human Resources 
At Coforge, our people strategy is a core driver of sustained 
growth, execution excellence, and our evolution into an AI-first, 
engineering-led organization. Anchored in our 4E framework – 
Examine, Engage, Educate, and Encourage – we focus on building 
a high-performance, future-ready workforce aligned to business 
priorities and client outcomes.
This talent strength, combined with deep specialization across AI, 
data, cloud, and domain-led engineering, enables the Company to 
consistently deliver complex, large-scale transformation programs 
and sustain strong deal momentum.
As of FY26, the Company employs a global workforce of over 
35,000+ professionals, supported by one of the lowest attrition 
rates in the industry at 10.8%, reflecting strong employee 
engagement and organizational stability. Our ability to attract, 
retain, and scale high-quality talent remains a key differentiator, 
particularly in niche areas such as AI, data engineering, cloud, and 
domain-led digital transformation.
Employee feedback remains central to our approach. Our annual 
engagement survey, “My Voice,” recorded a 82% participation rate, 
with satisfaction and commitment scores at 78%, indicating a 
stable and engaged workforce. Key drivers of engagement include 
strong teamwork, learning opportunities, managerial support, and organizational brand. These insights are actively leveraged to 
strengthen employee experience and retention.
We continue to foster an inclusive, high-engagement culture 
through structured initiatives focused on recognition, well-being, 
and collaboration. These are supported by transparent policies, 
multi-channel engagement, and a strong culture of coaching and 
development. Our efforts are reflected in continued external 
recognition, including certification as a “Great Place to Work” for the 
fifth consecutive year and inclusion among India’s Best Workplaces 
in IT & IT-BPM for 2025.
Capability development remains a strategic priority as we align 
our talent base to evolving technology landscapes. Our learning 
ecosystem, anchored in the AI-enabled Xcellerate Competency 
Framework and enterprise platforms such as iEnable, provides 
structured, role-based learning pathways across technical, domain, 
and leadership capabilities. The framework spans 800+ role-skill 
combinations linked to 1,200+ skills, enabling targeted and scalable 
workforce development.
During the year, the Company accelerated its AI-led capability-
building agenda. Key outcomes include training 15,500+ employees 
on AI programs, 14,000+ on GitHub, and 22,000+ certifications across 
hyperscalers and enterprise platforms. In addition, structured 
programs for campus hires and lateral talent ensured faster 
productivity ramp-up and alignment to delivery requirements. 
Overall, the Company delivered more than 1.39 million learning 
hours, with a strong emphasis on technical, domain, and functional 
skills.
Leadership development continued to be strengthened through 
structured programs across career stages, enabling the build-
out of a scalable leadership pipeline. In parallel, inclusion remains 
embedded in our culture through focused initiatives such as 
EmpowHER and structured return-to-work programs, reinforcing 
diversity, equity, and belonging across the organization.
Our people practices continue to receive strong external recognition 
across workplace culture, learning, inclusion, and employee 
development. These reflect Coforge’s continued commitment 
to building a resilient, high-quality talent base that is critical to 
delivering consistent business outcomes and sustaining long-term 
growth.
Together, these initiatives ensure that Coforge’s talent base 
not only scales with growth but also enhances delivery quality, 
productivity, and the ability to engineer measurable business 
outcomes for clients.

Opportunities, Risks and Concerns
Coforge enters FY27 with strong visibility into its medium-
term growth, supported by sustained enterprise demand for 
engineering-led, AI-enabled transformation across its core 
industries. The technology services landscape is undergoing a 
structural shift from effort-based delivery to outcome-oriented, 
AI-augmented engineering models. Enterprises are increasingly 
prioritizing platform modernization, improving the resilience of 
mission-critical systems, and optimizing long-term costs, areas 
where Coforge’s engineering-first approach, domain depth, and 
execution rigor provide a differentiated advantage. The Company’s 
expanding portfolio of large, multi-year transformation programs and managed services engagements enhances revenue visibility 
and strengthens the resilience of its operating model, even as 
enterprise decision cycles remain elongated. The Company’s FY26 
performance, strong order intake, and expanded executable order 
book provide additional confidence in this medium-term visibility.
A key opportunity lies in the rapid transition from experimental AI 
adoption to scaled, enterprise-wide deployment. As clients move 
beyond pilots toward embedding AI across engineering lifecycles, 
operations, and business workflows, demand is shifting toward 
partners capable of delivering AI-led transformation at scale with 
governance, reliability, and measurable outcomes. This transition 
is also redefining revenue models, as AI-driven systems require 
ongoing monitoring, optimization, and lifecycle management, 
creating a durable and high-value managed services layer. Coforge’s 
AI-embedded delivery model, supported by its proprietary 
platforms, accelerators, and engineering capabilities, positions 
the Company well to capture this structural shift while driving 
improvements in productivity, speed, and execution consistency.
In parallel, the continued expansion of GCCs, particularly across 
banking, financial services, insurance, healthcare, and hi-tech, 
presents a sustained opportunity aligned with Coforge’s strengths 
in domain-led engineering and managed services. GCCs are 
increasingly evolving into strategic innovation hubs rather than 
cost centers, driving long-duration, annuity-like engagements that 
provide both revenue stability and deeper client integration. This 
creates opportunities for Coforge to participate in build, operate, 
transform, and modernization programs where clients seek 
partners with a combination of domain knowledge, engineering 
depth, governance maturity, and execution scale.
The Company also sees opportunities from the increasing 
convergence of AI, data, cloud, quality engineering, and intelligent 
operations. As enterprises modernize legacy environments and 
prepare their technology estates for AI-led operating models, 
demand is expected to grow for integrated partners that 
can address data readiness, cloud foundations, engineering 
productivity, platform assurance, cybersecurity, and managed 
operations together. Coforge’s portfolio is aligned to this demand 
environment, with its AI-led engineering approach enabling 
clients to move from fragmented initiatives to enterprise-scale 
transformation programs.
While the opportunity environment remains attractive, Coforge 
operates in a dynamic global technology landscape where business, 
technology, financial, operational, and regulatory developments 
are monitored on an ongoing basis. These risks are consistent with 
the scale and nature of a global technology services business and 
are managed through established governance frameworks, strong 
delivery discipline, diversified client and sector exposure, robust 
information security practices, and continuous investments in 
talent and technology capabilities.
The macroeconomic environment remains uncertain in the near 
term. Geopolitical developments, interest rate volatility, currency 
fluctuations, and cautious enterprise spending in key markets 
such as North America and Europe may influence discretionary 
investments, deal conversion timelines, and program ramp-ups. 
However, Coforge’s focus on transformation-led, mission-critical, 
and regulated industry programs provides relative resilience, as 
clients continue to prioritize initiatives that improve efficiency, 
strengthen resilience, modernize core platforms, and deliver 
measurable business outcomes.
Coforge’s growth model is increasingly anchored in large, multi-year 
transformation and managed services engagements across core 
industries such as travel, banking and financial services, insurance, 
healthcare, retail, and the public sector. These engagements 
improve revenue visibility and deepen client partnerships, while also 
requiring strong governance around transition, ramp-up, delivery 
performance, service continuity, and client-specific execution. The Company addresses these priorities through structured deal 
governance, leadership oversight, disciplined execution reviews, 
transition planning, and continuous monitoring of delivery quality, 
productivity, and service performance.
Given the Company’s presence in regulated and mission-critical 
environments, operational resilience, service continuity, data 
privacy, security, and compliance remain key priorities. The 
growing adoption of cloud-native, AI-enabled, and interconnected 
enterprise architectures requires sustained focus on cybersecurity, 
data protection, model governance, responsible AI, and regulatory 
compliance. Coforge manages these priorities through robust 
information security frameworks, governance controls, compliance 
monitoring, redundancy planning, and continuous improvement of 
technology and delivery practices.
Rapid advancements in AI, automation, data, and cloud technologies 
also require continuous capability renewal. Demand for specialized 
skills in AI-led engineering, data platforms, cloud infrastructure, 
cybersecurity, and responsible AI continues to increase across 
the industry. Coforge addresses this through enterprise-wide 
upskilling, role-based learning programs, investments in platforms 
and accelerators, ecosystem partnerships, and ongoing capability 
development across engineering and delivery teams.
Financial and commercial risks, including currency movements, 
pricing pressure, changing client spending patterns, and evolving 
commercial models, are monitored through disciplined financial 
management. The Company seeks to mitigate these risks through 
geographic diversification, balanced portfolio management, cost 
discipline, structured deal reviews, financial hedging practices, and 
a focus on engagements where Coforge can deliver differentiated 
value through domain depth, engineering capability, and platform-
led execution.
Regulatory and governance requirements continue to evolve 
across geographies, particularly in areas such as data protection, 
cross-border operations, AI governance, cybersecurity, public 
sector procurement, and industry-specific compliance. Coforge 
maintains governance frameworks, internal controls, compliance 
processes, and localized delivery practices to support regulatory 
adherence while preserving operating flexibility.
Overall, Coforge’s response to this opportunity and risk 
environment is anchored in disciplined execution, portfolio 
balance, strong governance, and targeted investments in AI-led 
engineering capabilities. The Company continues to focus on 
vertical diversification, large-deal governance, productivity-led 
efficiency through platformization and AI adoption, enterprise-
wide upskilling, robust information security frameworks, proactive 
regulatory compliance, and financial discipline. By aligning its 
operating model with the industry’s shift toward outcome-driven 
and autonomous systems, Coforge remains well positioned to 
navigate near-term uncertainty while capturing the structural 
growth opportunity presented by AI-led enterprise transformation 
over the medium term.
The following section summarizes the key risk categories and the 
Company’s mitigation approach.
ESG and Sustainability
At Coforge, sustainability is embedded in the Company’s operating 
model as a core enabler of resilient, scalable growth, integrating 
responsible operations with people-centric development. Coforge’s 
ESG strategy is anchored in two reinforcing priorities: engineering-
led environmental efficiency and human capital transformation at 
scale, both of which directly contribute to long-term value creation 
and enterprise resilience. 
Environmental Sustainability
Coforge’s environmental strategy is distinguished by its focus on 
infrastructure-level optimization and engineering interventions.

AI-First Engineering | Architecting the Agentic  EnterpriseThis enables measurable reductions in energy consumption, 
emissions, and resource intensity as the Company scales its global 
delivery footprint.
During the year, targeted initiatives across core infrastructure 
resulted in tangible efficiency gains. At the Greater Noida campus, 
optimizing the backup infrastructure by right-sizing battery and 
diesel generation systems reduced the connected load by ~1,700 
KVA and annual electricity consumption by ~48,000 kWh, while 
significantly reducing the battery footprint and lowering hazardous 
waste and lifecycle emissions. 
In parallel, the transition from R22 to R32 refrigerants reflects 
a proactive shift toward lower global warming potential (GWP) 
systems, aligned with evolving environmental regulations and 
long-term emissions reduction goals.
A key milestone in the Company’s sustainability journey is the 
transition of its Greater Noida campus to 100% renewable 
electricity, demonstrating the viability of large-scale adoption of 
clean energy within enterprise technology operations. This has 
contributed to a reduction in Scope 2 emissions, complemented 
by Scope 1 mitigation through infrastructure and refrigerant 
optimization. 
Water Stewardship and Circular Resource Management
Coforge continues to embed resource efficiency and circularity in 
operational systems, with a focus on water conservation, waste 
reduction, and sustainable workplace practices.
Water management initiatives have delivered structural efficiency 
improvements, including reduced per-use consumption through 
optimized fixtures, sensor-based systems, and automated overflow 
controls to minimize losses. Treated water reuse through sewage 
treatment infrastructure supports non-potable applications, such 
as landscaping, thereby reducing overall freshwater demand. 
The Company has also advanced its transition toward circular waste 
management by eliminating single-use plastics, implementing 
enterprise-wide waste segregation, and installing in-house 
composting systems, reducing reliance on landfills while improving 
recycling efficiency and employee participation in sustainable 
practices. 
Sustainable Mobility and Forward-Looking Priorities
Sustainable mobility initiatives, including transitioning 
approximately 7% of the Company’s fleet to electric vehicles and 
establishing EV charging infrastructure, reflect a broader effort to 
reduce indirect emissions associated with employee commuting 
and operations. 
Looking ahead, the Company remains focused on scaling renewable 
energy adoption, completing the elimination of residual single-use 
plastics, and expanding energy efficiency interventions, reinforcing 
its commitment to long-term environmental sustainability. Human Capital as a Strategic Differentiator
Coforge’s people strategy is designed as a scalable, capability-led 
system that aligns workforce development with business growth 
and technology evolution. The Company has institutionalized data-
driven talent architecture, enabling precision in skill mapping, 
deployment, and career progression across a rapidly evolving 
technology landscape. 
Platforms like Xcellerate support this model by structuring 
the mapping of 800+ role-skill combinations and 1,200+ skills, 
ensuring alignment between talent supply and demand. This 
is complemented by structured onboarding and deployment 
programs that deliver a ~90% train-to-deployment conversion 
rate, significantly accelerating workforce productivity. 
AI-Enabled Workforce and Continuous Capability Building
The Company is advancing toward an AI-enabled workforce model, 
integrating AI into learning, development, and delivery systems. 
Large-scale enablement initiatives, including 14,000+ GitHub 
Copilot certifications, demonstrate the rapid scaling of AI-ready 
talent across the organization. 
This upskilling enables Coforge to enhance engineering throughput, 
improve delivery efficiency, and build a workforce that continuously 
evolves in alignment with emerging technology paradigms.
Workforce Resilience, Engagement, and Retention
Coforge has established structured support systems to enhance 
employee well-being and long-term engagement, including 
financial and psychological safety mechanisms such as the 
Employee Welfare Trust and the Employee Assistance Program. 
These initiatives provide comprehensive support across health, 
financial, and life-stage needs, strengthening workforce resilience. 
These efforts are reflected in strong organizational metrics, 
including 11.6% attrition and a net promoter score (NPS) of 65, 
indicating high levels of employee advocacy and stability in a 
competitive talent environment.

BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE COMPANY’S WORKING 
DURING THE YEAR AND STATE OF THE COMPANY’S 
AFFAIRS
Operating highlights
Fiscal Year 2026 has been a year of continued strong growth for 
Coforge. The Company registered a consolidated US$ revenue of 
US$1,870 million (INR. 164,027 million) and has clocked a revenue 
growth of 29.2% in $ terms and 35.9% in INR terms.
The year saw Coforge sign twenty one large deals, five of which 
were signed during the recent quarter, i.e., Q4FY26. On the back 
of twenty one large deals signed through the year, the total 
order intake (TCV) for FY 2026 reached US$2.3 billion. Coforge’s 
investment in sales and marketing, despite challenging market 
conditions, has resulted in an increasing velocity and median size 
of the large contracts it has signed during the year.
Financial highlights
Effective FY26, realized cash flow hedge gains/losses are 
reclassified from revenue to forex gain/loss within other income/
expense to align with peer practice and isolating revenue and EBIT 
margins from forex movements, with PBT and PAT unchanged and 
all comparatives restated. 
On a consolidated basis, revenues increased 35.9% to INR 164,027 
million in FY2026 from INR 120,733 million in FY2025. The growth 
was led by the Travel vertical, which saw 70.7% YoY growth followed 
by Healthcare and Hi-Tech which saw 109% YoY growth. Banking and Financial Services vertical grew by 18.0%, Insurance vertical 
grew 10.1%, Govt. outside India vertical grew 23.2% and the other 
emerging verticals, including manufacturing and retail, grew 34.2% 
For the full year FY26, the Company’s gross margin was 33.8%. 
EBITDA stood at INR 30,464 million, translating into a margin of 
18.6% for the year. EBIT stood at INR 23,645 million, translating 
into a margin of 14.4% for the year. EBIT margin for the year 
increased by 370 bps YoY.
The net profits (attributable to the equity holders of the parent 
including discontinued operations) for the year stood at INR 
15,557 million.
During the financial year, the company added a net of 2,754 
professionals to its headcount, thus taking its total headcount to 
35,777 at the end of FY26.
The above operating and financial highlights relate to 
continuing operations.

Acquisition of Encora Group and issuance and allotment of 
Equity Shares on a Preferential Basis pursuant to a Share 
Swap Arrangement
The Company entered into a share subscription and share purchase 
agreement (“SSPA”) dated December 26, 2025 with Encora US 
Holdco, Inc. and Encora Holdings Ltd. (Cayman) (collectively, the 
“Target Companies”), Encora Holdco Ltd. (UK) and AI Altius Parent 
(Cayman) Limited (collectively, the “Investors”) in relation to the 
acquisition of the Target Companies’ shares from the Investors 
through a share swap arrangement (“Proposed Acquisition”). In 
terms of the SSPA, up to 9,37,96,508 (Nine Crore Thirty Seven 
Lakh Ninety Six Thousand Five Hundred and Eight) fully paid-up 
equity shares of the Company having face value of INR 2 each 
(“Equity Shares”) are proposed to be created, issued, offered 
and allotted to the Investors at an issue price of INR 1,815.91 
per Equity Share (including a premium of INR 1,813.91 per Equity 
Share), aggregating up to a consideration of INR 1,70,32,60,16,842, 
in accordance with the terms of the SSPA.
The shareholders of the Company approved the aforesaid 
transaction, including issuance of equity shares on a preferential 
basis pursuant to the share swap arrangement, by way of postal 
ballot concluded on January 25, 2026.
The transaction was subject to receipt of requisite regulatory 
approvals across multiple jurisdictions. During the year, the Company obtained key approvals, including clearance under the 
Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act in the United 
States, competition approvals in relevant jurisdictions including 
Australia, and approval from the Reserve Bank of India for 
overseas direct investment exceeding USD 1 billion under the 
Foreign Exchange Management (Overseas Investment) Rules.
Subsequently, on April 10, 2026, the Company received in-principle 
approvals from the stock exchanges for the preferential issue. 
Pursuant thereto, the Company allotted 9,37,96,508 Equity 
Shares of face value INR 2 each at an issue price of INR 1,815.91 
per Equity Share on April 23, 2026 in accordance with the terms 
of the SSPA. The Preferential Issue was carried out in compliance 
with the applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and the 
rules made thereunder, Chapter V of the Securities and Exchange 
Board of India (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2018, the Foreign Exchange Management (Non-Debt 
Instrument) Rules, 2019, and other applicable laws.
The Company filed an application with the stock exchanges on April 
24, 2026 seeking listing approval for the said Equity Shares and 
subsequently received such approval. The Company has completed 
the allotment and is undertaking the necessary post-closing and 
regulatory compliances in accordance with applicable laws.
Approval for grant of special rights and covenants 
pursuant to the SSPA
The Board of Directors approved the revised proposal under the 
Share Subscription and Share Purchase Agreement (“SSPA”), as 
amended, for the grant of certain special rights and covenants 
to the investors, namely Encora Holdco Ltd. (UK) and AI Altius 
Parent (Cayman) Limited (“Investors”). In this regard, the Company, 
together with Encora US Holdco, Inc. and Encora Holdings Ltd. 
(collectively, the “Target Companies”), entered into an amendment 
agreement dated January 28, 2026 to the SSPA executed on 
December 26, 2025 to record revised terms, relating to the fall-
away thresholds for the Investors’ right to nominate directors on 
the Board. The revised proposal was subsequently approved by 
the shareholders of the Company on February 27, 2026.
Under the amended terms, the Investors are entitled to nominate 
upto two nominee directors on the Board, subject to prescribed 
shareholding thresholds. The right to appoint two nominee 
directors shall continue so long as the aggregate shareholding 
of the Investors remains above 15% of the share capital of the 
Company, shall reduce to one nominee director if such shareholding 
falls below 15%, and shall cease entirely if such shareholding falls 
below 10%. The right to appoint nominee directors on Board 
committees has been removed, and no amendments to the Articles 
of Association of the Company are proposed in respect of such 
rights as may be required approved ancillary actions. Subsequent 
to the financial year end, upon completion of Encora acquisition 
on April 23, 2026, the Company did not proceed with the QIP and 
instead secured a USD 550 million three-year term loan facility 
at a fixed interest rate of 4.6% per annum from a consortium of 
international lenders to retire the debt in Encora. The shareholder 
resolution authorising the QIP remains valid but the Company does 
not currently intend to utilize it.
In the opinion of the Board, the aforesaid approval is in the best 
interest of the Company and its stakeholders.

Limited with the Company and their respective 
Shareholders and Creditors
At its meeting held on December 27, 2024, the Board of Directors 
approved the Scheme of Amalgamation of Cigniti Technologies 
Limited (“Cigniti”) with and into Coforge Limited and their 
respective shareholders and creditors under Sections 230 to 232 
and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, read 
with the rules made thereunder (“Scheme”). The Scheme, inter 
alia, provides for the amalgamation of Cigniti, as the transferor 
company, with and into the Company. Pursuant to the proposed 
Scheme, as amended post-split of Coforge Limited’s shares and 
duly approved by the Board of Directors on July 06, 2025, one fully 
paid-up equity share of the Company of INR 2 each are issued to 
the shareholders of Cigniti for every one fully paid-up equity share 
of INR 10 each held by them. On January 10, 2025, the Company 
filed the Scheme with the stock exchanges and SEBI and received 
their approval.
Pursuant to the order dated October 17, 2025 passed by the 
Hon’ble National Company Law Tribunal (“NCLT”), separate court-
convened meetings of the equity shareholders, secured creditors 
and unsecured creditors of the Company were held on December 
06, 2025 through Video Conferencing / Other Audio Visual Means in 
connection with the proposed Scheme. The meetings were chaired 
by Mr. L. N. Gupta (IAS) (Retd.), former Member, NCLT, as appointed 
by the Hon’ble Tribunal. Mr. Yashraj Singh, Advocate, appointed as 
the Scrutinizer by the Hon’ble NCLT, was present at the meetings. 
The requisite quorum being present, the meetings were duly 
conducted in accordance with the NCLT order and applicable legal 
and regulatory requirements, and the Scheme was approved by 
the requisite majority.
Thereafter, the Hon’ble NCLT, Chandigarh Bench, by its order dated 
April 29, 2026, approved the Scheme. The certified copy of the 
order has been filed with the Registrar of Companies, Haryana, and 
all conditions specified under the Scheme have been complied with. 
Accordingly, the Scheme has become effective and the transferor 
company stands amalgamated with and into the Company and 
dissolved without being wound up, with the appointed date being 
April 01, 2025.
The Scheme has received all requisite statutory and regulatory 
approvals, including approvals from the stock exchanges, the 
Securities and Exchange Board of India, the shareholders and 
creditors of the respective companies, and the Hon’ble National 
Company Law Tribunal. Pursuant to the Scheme, the Board of 
Directors fixed May 16, 2026 as the record date for determining the 
shareholders of the transferor company whose equity shares shall 
stand cancelled and to whom new equity shares of the Company 
shall be issued in accordance with the 1:1 share exchange ratio.
The Scheme was intended to enhance operational integration 
and streamline the corporate structure. By pooling resources, 
sharing best practices and fostering cross-functional learning, 
the amalgamation was expected to improve systemic efficiency 
and eliminate redundancies, including duplicate workstreams 
and administrative overheads. This reduction in operating costs, 
enabling seamless access to assets and strengthening cash flow management, thereby supporting the sustained growth 
and development of the combined business. The scheme also 
facilitated market expansion, created cross-selling opportunities 
and drove operational efficiencies through consolidated processes 
and shared services. In addition, it also fostered innovation 
through the pooling of technological resources and talent, while 
enabling more efficient management of the combined entity’s 
operations. The Scheme ensured that the rights and interests of 
employees and shareholders of both Coforge and Cigniti remain 
unaffected and aligns with the objective of creating long-term 
value for stakeholders.
In the view of the Board, the Scheme is fair and reasonable and is 
not detrimental to the shareholders (promoter and non-promoter 
shareholders), key managerial personnel, staff or employees of the 
Company, and no prejudice shall be caused to them in any manner 
by the Scheme.

DPA UK Limited, step-down wholly owned subsidiaries of the 
Company, in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations 
of the United Kingdom.
These entities are not engaged in any active business operations, 
and the proposed winding-up / strike-off is intended as a strategic 
rationalisation measure to streamline the group structure. This 
initiative is expected to enhance operational synergy, reduce 
administrative overheads and improve cost efficiency across the 
Company’s business operations in the United Kingdom.
The voluntary winding up / strike off process shall be carried out 
in compliance with the applicable legal, regulatory and statutory 
requirements of the respective jurisdiction. There is no material 
impact of the aforesaid restructuring on the financial position 
or operations of the Company. The Company will complete all 
requisite filings and compliances as may be required under 
applicable laws.

Policies of the Company
Those Charged with Governance (TCWG) framework
To enhance audit quality, strengthen governance oversight, 
and ensure compliance with the Companies Act, 2013 and 
Standards on Auditing (SA 260 (Revised) and SA 265), and in line 
with the NFRA Circular dated January 07, 2026 a policy on Two-Way Communication Between Those Charged with Governance 
(TCWG) and the Statutory Auditors was recently adopted by the 
Board. This Policy applies to audit of the Company’s standalone 
and consolidated financial statements and review of quarterly 
standalone and consolidated financial results and covers:
• Two-way communications between Auditors and TCWG and 
other duly empowered sub groups of Board.
• Communication of audit strategy, audit plan, scope, timing, 
materiality, key risks, significant judgments/estimates, 
independence, internal financial controls in particular to prevent 
frauds and non-compliance with critical laws and regulations, 
identified control deficiencies, areas of significant accounting 
policy judgment and management estimations; areas requiring 
involvement of experts, either by the Management or the 
Auditors, regulatory non compliances, significant unusual 
transactions, and going concern matters.
The members of the Audit Committee, CEO, and CFO of the 
Company are members of the TCWG, and the Company Secretary is 
an invitee to the TCWG. One meeting of the TCWG was held on May 
4, 2026, in the presence of the Statutory Auditors of the Company.
